open_questions: Which ACK wire layout is authoritative for the product after the S2 seam swap: engine §2 ACK_FRAME_V2 0x14 (u16 seq, 15 B + 4 B/range, currently on the wire under IdentitySeam) or noise-wire §2.57 Control::Ack 0x10 (u64 pn ranges, 11 B + 16 B/range) / Control::Sack 0x11? The 65 B `sack_wire` constant that feeds EAI, ACK_CADENCE_FLOOR, T_SPACING, W_BTLBW return-prior and PreConverge RTT_floor assumes the engine layout under a 22 B hop header.

Is §3.3-E FULL (measured return_bw replacing the 31 B/s prior on both receiver cadence and sender EAI) inside v1 scope? The spec labels it ADIM-6/E-FULL debt, yet sender.rs:611-621 and bench main.rs:76-77 document that the static prior makes the loss-ledger confirm horizon never fire on the product path (16×RTT at 200 ms). Who owns the estimator (receiver lacks datagram size; sender-side ACK-spacing estimate?).

ACK decimation (reverse-path-impaired ACK_FREQ↑/budget↓) is deferred to ADIM-6 by §3.3-E, but TDD AC-8 requires 'sparse cumulative ACK' in EMERGENCY. Is the static cadence floor accepted as satisfying AC-8, or is a sender→receiver decimation signal a v1 requirement? emergency.rs:205 ack_decimation() has no product consumer.

Cross-epoch ACK rejection (engine §2 L155-156, NORMATİF) is unimplemented; ack_epoch is constant 0 on both ends and never read by the sender. Is this formally deferred to S2 rekey, and should the sender's `ack_epoch = max(srtt, EAI)` time-window variable be renamed to avoid collision with the wire epoch?

K_TAIL (receiver.rs:100, tail-SACK exemption) is a time-comparing constant not registered in the §16.1 [CAL] table; ZM-3 says an unregistered class is CI-red grounds. Spec omission or intentional (it is channel-derived)?

ack_confidence anchor: code uses last_ack_ns.or(first_send_ns) (sender.rs:5802) while §5.1 specifies max(last_ack_time, first_send_time) and §16.2 lists this as an unfixed SUSPECT row ('idle-resume'da bayat anchor → anında RecoverFwd'). Is there an owner decision to keep or fix?

Receiver audit counters required/implied by the spec (ack_delay_saturated §2.1; K-4 invariant quota_emits ≤ R×episode_count via diag_return_supply; sender diag_rtt rejected/max_ack_delay) are not surfaced through ServerStats/ClientStats, so kama-product runs cannot observe them (only the legacy bench kama.rs arm reads them). Telemetry gap or intentional?

Receiver never waits within a reordering threshold before reporting a gap (§4 'RX_REORDER (bekle)'); receiver.rs:8-11 declares this a deliberate SoC choice with sender-side tolerance (§9.3). Does the owner accept §4's wording as informational?

SACK-V2 measurement ext consumer (seen≪sent direction split, arrival_rate cold-start hint, 'K3') was never wired and the equivalent CS-echo fields are declared ledger-only/decision-forbidden (noise-wire §2.57). Is the SACK-V2 consumer still planned, or are the 6 B/ACK fields now dead weight kept only for wire-format stability?

client-core is unidirectional (ClientEndpoint has no Receiver; ServerEndpoint never emits DATA). Hop-by-hop reliability in the hub→client direction (and therefore client-emitted SACKs) does not exist in the product runtime — is that in v1 scope?

Receiver/sender 'mirror constants' (ACK_FREQ_N=2 vs EXPECTED_ACK_FREQ_N=2; 65 B and 31 B/s in receiver.rs:76-87, sender.rs:1393-1397, sender.rs:1455, and the literal 2_097_000_000 ns at sender.rs:2907) are hand-duplicated with no shared definition — acceptable, or should a single const module bind them (drift risk when return_bw becomes measured)?
sender.rs:2897-2912 computes `ack_epoch` in on_ack_received and discards it (`let _ = ack_epoch;`) — dead code candidate.

Tail-PTO max_ack_delay_ns=25 ms (validated_v1) vs receiver's legitimate timer-SACK hold of up to 8.39 s at sub-kbps: validated only on the DR-ARQ-PRODUCT-TAIL-1 grid; does the sub-kbps regime produce spurious tail probes, and should max_ack_delay be derived from the receiver cadence model (ZM-4)?

Legacy bench `kama` arm (bench/src/kama.rs) re-implements the server ACK loop (ACK_TICK, Receiver, decode) in parallel with client-core server_task and is the only consumer of several receiver diag accessors — retire it or keep as reference driver?
Divergent range caps: engine MAX_ACK_RANGES=16 [CAL] vs noise-wire ACK_MAX_RANGES=32 / SACK_MAX_GAP_BLOCKS=32 (DR-1 Abkarada-onaylı) — which bound applies to the product ACK after S2?
